suites.note: Six React checks carry five of these eleven: the retire, channels and unsubscribe routes, the supervision mode and outbox counts as returned, the watch and delivery rows, and the token on every request. No React control exists yet for the outbox acknowledgement, the coordinate create form, the per-place aggregate or a per-watch push binding.

tests: renders the kept brief with the time it was kept, the source it named and the no-delivery sentence the store returned
reads an opened brief through the token-authenticated store route and shows the limits and hash stored with it
deletes only after a stated confirmation, names the brief, and re-reads the list rather than assuming
says nothing is kept when the store is empty, and invents no entry
asks the server to compose a brief for a resolved point rather than posting a brief body itself

suites.note: The vanilla check bundles ten sub-rules into one PASS, and five of them are held by the parity spec (kept entries with their no-delivery sentence, the token-authenticated open, delete after a stated confirmation, the empty store, and the compose request). The whole check is not carried: no export control and no briefing-series surface exist in the React frontend, so the integer stays 0 rather than claiming a pass.

Not claimed: this suite checks the geometry of web/viz.js, which the React build is served from its one tracked copy at /viz.js, so the same checks still run against the same bytes (pinned by tests/test_react_vendor_assets.py). Claiming them as ported would be false; retiring them would drop nine checks that still pass against the served engine.
